rules.title: Reservation followed by cancellation within {{within_s}} s
rules.description: A reservation workflow was followed by a cancellation in the same tab after {{duration_s}} s (events seq {{first_seq}}–{{last_seq}}).
rules.possible_explanation: Commonly a deliberate test step, the correction of a mistaken reservation, or part of a scripted replay.
rules.recommended_next_test: Replay the RESERVATION → CANCELLATION segment on the mock (draft: GET /v1/sessions/{{session_id}}/workflow) with a longer pause between the two steps and compare the recorded sequences.
counter_evidence: Creating and cancelling test reservations is an expected activity in the mock environment.

rules.title: Rate change shortly before a reservation
rules.description: A rate-setup workflow was followed by a reservation workflow after {{duration_s}} s (events seq {{first_seq}}–{{last_seq}}).
rules.possible_explanation: Rates are often adjusted right before testing a booking flow; the two steps may simply be part of one test plan.
rules.recommended_next_test: Replay the reservation with and without the preceding rate change on the mock and compare the reservation totals and timings.

rules.title: Same control activated {{count}} times in {{duration_s}} s
rules.description: The control {{pattern}} was activated {{count}} times in a row within {{within_s}} s.
rules.possible_explanation: Repeated activation often means the page gave no visible feedback, a double submit, or an intentional retry.
rules.recommended_next_test: Replay the step once on the mock with a waitFor on the expected confirmation element and measure the time until it appears.
counter_evidence: Some controls (pagination, +/- steppers) are designed to be pressed repeatedly.

rules.title: Action sequence repeated {{count}} times
rules.description: A sequence of {{length}} operator actions recurred {{count}} times: {{pattern}}.
rules.possible_explanation: Typical of batch data entry, a retry loop after an unexpected result, or a replayed script.
rules.recommended_next_test: Compare the timing of each repetition in the Timeline view, then replay one iteration on the mock and check whether its outcome differs from the others.

rules.title: Idle period of {{gap_s}} s
rules.description: No events were recorded for {{gap_s}} s (threshold {{threshold_s}} s) between seq {{first_seq}} and {{last_seq}}.
rules.possible_explanation: The operator paused, switched to another application, or worked in a tab outside the recordable scope.
rules.recommended_next_test: Check whether the workflow continued in another tab; re-run the same workflow without the pause on the mock and compare the recorded sequences.

rules.title: No page update observed after an action
rules.description: No page change ({{expected}}) was recorded within {{within_s}} s after {{pattern}}.
rules.possible_explanation: The action may have had no visible effect, the page may update outside the observed attributes, or the response was slower than the window.
rules.recommended_next_test: Replay the action on the mock with waitFor on the expected confirmation element and a 10 s timeout; compare with the recorded timing.
counter_evidence: DOM observation covers structure and selected attributes only; text-only updates are not recorded.

rules.title: {{workflow}} completed in {{duration_s}} s
rules.description: The {{workflow}} segment with {{count}} events lasted {{duration_s}} s (below {{threshold_s}} s).
rules.possible_explanation: Very short segments are typical of prepared test data, browser autofill, or a replayed workflow.
rules.recommended_next_test: Open the Compare view for this workflow across sessions; replay it on the mock at a manual pace and compare durations.

rules.title: {{workflow}} lasted {{duration_s}} s
rules.description: The {{workflow}} segment lasted {{duration_s}} s (above {{threshold_s}} s).
rules.possible_explanation: Long segments often include reading, waiting for other people, or leaving the page open while doing something else.
rules.recommended_next_test: Inspect the idle gaps inside this segment in the Timeline view; replay the segment on the mock without pauses and compare step timings.

rules.title: {{count}} error event(s) recorded
rules.description: The recording contains {{count}} event(s) with severity error.
rules.possible_explanation: Page or extension errors; they may also affect what the recording captured around them.
rules.recommended_next_test: Open each error in the event drawer, then reproduce the workflow on the mock and check whether the same error recurs at the same step.

rules.title: {{count}} operator actions within {{window_s}} s
rules.description: {{count}} clicks or field changes were recorded within {{window_s}} s.
rules.possible_explanation: Fast data entry, browser autofill filling several fields at once, or a replayed script.
rules.recommended_next_test: Check in the event drawer which fields were involved; enter the same data manually on the mock and compare the action rate.
counter_evidence: Autofill of address or login forms routinely produces several field changes within a second.

rules.title: High page-update rate ({{count}} summaries in {{window_s}} s)
rules.description: {{count}} DOM-change summaries were recorded within {{window_s}} s.
rules.possible_explanation: Live-updating widgets, polling feeds, animations or repeated re-rendering.
rules.recommended_next_test: Open the DOM-change events to see which selectors changed most; compare with the same view in another session.

rules.title: Unusually long pause of {{gap_s}} s
rules.description: A pause of {{gap_s}} s is an outlier among this session's gaps (robust z = {{z}}).
rules.possible_explanation: An interruption, reading time, or waiting for a slow page; outliers are relative to this session only.
rules.recommended_next_test: Inspect the events around the pause in the Timeline view; replay the surrounding steps on the mock to see whether the page itself is slow at this step.

rules.title: {{workflow}} duration differs from other sessions
rules.description: This {{workflow}} segment lasted {{duration_s}} s, an outlier against {{count}} segments of the same workflow in other sessions (robust z = {{z}}).
rules.possible_explanation: Different data, a different path through the workflow, or interruptions; the baseline sessions may not be comparable.
rules.recommended_next_test: Open the Compare view against a typical session and check which steps account for the difference.

rules.title: Tab left the recordable scope {{count}} time(s)
rules.description: A recorded tab navigated to an origin outside the recordable scope {{count}} time(s); activity there is not recorded by design.
rules.possible_explanation: The operator followed an external link or opened another site in the same tab.
rules.recommended_next_test: If the workflow continued elsewhere and you are authorized to observe it, add that exact origin in the extension Options and record again.

rules.title: Sensitive fields used {{count}} time(s)
rules.description: {{count}} interaction(s) with password, one-time-code or payment fields were recorded structurally; their values were not read.
rules.possible_explanation: Login or payment steps are part of the workflow.
rules.recommended_next_test: When replaying, supply these fields as secret parameters at run time; they are never stored.

rules.title: {{count}} gap(s) in the event sequence
rules.description: The sequence numbers of this session contain {{count}} gap(s).
rules.possible_explanation: A service-worker restart (sequence resumes 1000 higher by design), events still queued in the extension, or queue-overflow drops.
rules.recommended_next_test: Check the extension popup's queued and dropped counters, flush, and run the analysis again.

rules.title: {{count}} event payload(s) quarantined
rules.description: {{count}} event payload(s) were replaced by the service because they still looked sensitive after redaction.
rules.possible_explanation: Recorded metadata contained an email, a long digit run or a large number (for example a timestamp inside metadata).
rules.recommended_next_test: Inspect which actions were quarantined in the event drawer and adjust what the recorder puts in metadata; record again.

rules.title: Timestamps moved backwards {{count}} time(s)
rules.description: Event timestamps decreased by more than 1 s while sequence numbers increased ({{count}} time(s)).
rules.possible_explanation: A system clock adjustment (manual change, time sync or time-zone change) during recording.
rules.recommended_next_test: Order by sequence number rather than time for this session; record again after confirming the system clock is stable.

rules.title: Session has no recorded end
rules.description: Neither a session_end event nor an end time was recorded for this session.
rules.possible_explanation: Recording is still running, the browser closed while recording, or the final events are still queued in the extension.
rules.recommended_next_test: Stop the recording from the popup (or flush it) and run the analysis again.

rules.title: {{count}} workflow transition(s) shared with other sessions
rules.description: Transitions in this session that also appear in at least half of the {{sessions_total}} analysed sessions: {{pattern}}.
rules.possible_explanation: Common paths through these workflows; co-occurrence across sessions describes the data set, not any outcome.
rules.recommended_next_test: Compare this session with one that lacks these transitions (Compare view) to see which steps differ.

rules.title: {{count}} transition(s) rare across analysed sessions
rules.description: Transitions in this session that appear in at most a quarter of the {{sessions_total}} analysed sessions: {{pattern}}.
rules.possible_explanation: This session took a path that other sessions rarely took: different test data, a different task, or an unusual detour.
rules.recommended_next_test: Open the Compare view against a typical session; replay the rare path on the mock to check whether it behaves like the common one.
counter_evidence: Rarity depends on which sessions were analysed; a small or unrepresentative cohort makes ordinary paths look rare.
